task: independent audit of the Gaussian output-sampling lemma
scope: ideal-real probability theorem and N687 whole-vector oracle compatibility; no N687 polylogarithmic-in-dimension theorem or oracle lower bound claimed

proved_claims.independent_coordinate_identity: chi2(Law(m+V+Z)||N(m,sigma^2 I)) = product_i E exp(V_i V_i'/sigma^2) - 1

N687_whole_vector_sampler.algorithm: draw k iid G_j~N(0,I), query X_j=g(G_j), return mean(X_j)+independent N(0,sigma^2 I)
N687_whole_vector_sampler.count_floor: at least one query to reveal an unknown constant field when L=0
N687_whole_vector_sampler.arithmetic: O(k d), O(d) streaming storage, exact-real model

proved_claims.rare_independent_bumps: |X_i|<=A w and P(X_i!=0)<=C w imply exponent O(d w^6); w=d^(-1/4) yields TV O(d^(-1/4)) while ||E X||2 can remain O(1)

application_limits: Added Gaussian noise is sampler postprocessing; the raw exact N687 oracle response is not thereby hidden or noisy.
The comparison Gaussian retains the unknown mean m, so the result alone does not make distinct target means statistically indistinguishable.
The rare-coordinate product estimate requires coordinate independence; arbitrary N687 fields need not satisfy it.
The generic subGaussian route costs O(1+(L^2/sigma^2) sqrt(d)/epsilon), not polylogarithmic in d.
Finite-bit Gaussian generation, oracle rounding and arithmetic are not certified; use a commonly quantized target for TV statements.
prior_art: N722 in the pinned capital already records sample-mean-plus-Gaussian smoothing for a known-bounded iid vector oracle and identifies stochastic FORS as the stronger comparator. Nielsen and Nock (2013), arXiv:1309.3029, give closed-form chi-square distances for same-exponential-family distributions, including isotropic Gaussians; this is related background for the Gaussian location-family calculation, not a claim of the exact random-mixture/proxy bound. The exact N687 interface mismatch remains: g(G) is generally unbounded and N687 states an every-execution active value-query model.

validation.scope: one-dimensional density quadrature, finite product enumeration, Gaussian proxy identity, exact query threshold, explicit gradient rare-bump integrals, and correlated rare-marginal counterexample
validation.proof_status: the general inequalities are derived in proof/DERIVATION.md; numerical checks are sanity checks, not substitutes for proof
